decision_statements_in_order.text: The export and its worksheet point to a potentially shared experimental source. Check the cited table, assay context and strain provenance in the supplied study materials before accepting W1 as an additional measurement. Does the cited Ima3p table entry identify an independent specific activity, and which assay, protein and strain fields does the study document?

BRENDA 2026.1 row 3.2.1.10/specific_activity/59 gives 3.9 for the yeast enzyme on α-pNPG at pH 7 and 30 °C and links PMID 24649402. Its unit and strain fields are blank. Publisher return E2 for Deng et al., FEBS Open Bio 4 (2014), 200–212, DOI 10.1016/j.fob.2014.02.004, PMCID PMC3953731, Table 2 (JATS t0010), gives “3.9 (54)” and “7.2 (100)” in the Ima3p column for α-pNPG and isomaltose. The heading supplies μmol/min/mg. The note identifies the denominator, conditions and mean of five experiments. The ratio 100 × 3.9/7.2 rounds to 54%. The Introduction (s0005) identifies S288c as genome context. Experimental procedures (s0080) identify CEN.PK113-5D as expression host. Publish a single α-pNPG result. Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ima3p (archive accession P0CW40) had a mean specific activity of 3.9 μmol/min/mg with 5 mM 4-nitrophenyl α-D-glucopyranoside at pH 7.0 and 30 °C (five experiments). Retain W1’s 54 as relative velocity in percent of the same enzyme’s isomaltose value (7.2 μmol/min/mg = 100%). W1 adds zero independent measurements. Remove the S288C strain assignment, leave the source strain unknown and record CEN.PK113-5D in the expression-host field.

question: A curator of food-yeast records wants to publish the worksheet entry alongside the archive entry. Should its measurement, evidence count, assay conditions, protein and strain fields be kept, corrected, or left unknown? Give the curator concise publishable wording and the original scientific locators. Use only this study's supplied records. A publisher return may arrive while the question is open. Read the supplied archive record itself before closing and revise as warranted. Additional evidence may justify keeping the provisional judgement.
report:
Publish a single α-pNPG result. Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ima3p (archive accession P0CW40) had a mean specific activity of 3.9 μmol/min/mg with 5 mM 4-nitrophenyl α-D-glucopyranoside at pH 7.0 and 30 °C (five experiments). Retain W1’s 54 as relative velocity in percent of the same enzyme’s isomaltose value (7.2 μmol/min/mg = 100%). W1 adds zero independent measurements. Remove the S288C strain assignment, leave the source strain unknown and record CEN.PK113-5D in the expression-host field.

BRENDA 2026.1 row 3.2.1.10/specific_activity/59 gives 3.9 for the yeast enzyme on α-pNPG at pH 7 and 30 °C and links PMID 24649402. Its unit and strain fields are blank. Publisher return E2 for Deng et al., FEBS Open Bio 4 (2014), 200–212, DOI 10.1016/j.fob.2014.02.004, PMCID PMC3953731, Table 2 (JATS t0010), gives “3.9 (54)” and “7.2 (100)” in the Ima3p column for α-pNPG and isomaltose. The heading supplies μmol/min/mg. The note identifies the denominator, conditions and mean of five experiments. The ratio 100 × 3.9/7.2 rounds to 54%. The Introduction (s0005) identifies S288c as genome context. Experimental procedures (s0080) identify CEN.PK113-5D as expression host.

The assayed protein’s native source strain is unspecified.

rubric.conditions: Correctly reports pH 7, 30 °C and the 5 mM pNPG condition when describing the measurement.
rubric.counterevidence: Correctly interprets 3.9 μmol/min/mg and 54 percent as two representations of the same result and rejects counting the worksheet number as another independent measurement.
rubric.locator: Identifies BRENDA 3.2.1.10/specific_activity/59 and the identifiable paper plus its Table 2.
rubric.protein: Attributes the measurement to the published Ima3p column and the archive's P0CW40 entry within the supplied evidence.
rubric.strain: Distinguishes the reported CEN.PK113-5D expression host from the S288c genome and avoids attributing the experiment to an S288C culture.
rubric.substrate: Identifies α-pNPG as the substrate of the scrutinized value, and isomaltose as the denominator for relative activity.
rubric.uncertainty: Distinguishes the original five-experiment summary from the number of independently sourced result records, and avoids inferring unreported per-replicate values.
